recognize_zh: 左圖 Wright 染色見大量紅血球含成簇、細小不規則的紫色顆粒（Pappenheimer bodies），並有標靶細胞、棘狀與不規則紅血球；右圖普魯士藍（Perls）鐵染色顯示同樣顆粒呈藍色（siderocytes），證實為含鐵顆粒，脾切除使其大量出現在周邊血。
features: Wright stain: many red cells with small clusters of irregular basophilic granules, often at the cell periphery (Pappenheimer bodies)
Target cells, acanthocyte-like and irregularly shaped red cells
Occasional red cell with a single round dense inclusion suggestive of a Howell-Jolly body
Prussian blue stain: dark blue siderotic granules within numerous red cells (siderocytes)
Frequency of inclusions is much higher than expected with an intact spleen
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (Wright stain) shows numerous erythrocytes containing clusters of small irregular basophilic granules, along with target cells, acanthocyte-like forms and irregular poikilocytes. A Prussian blue stain on the same specimen shows these inclusions as dark blue iron-positive granules, confirming siderocytes. In a splenectomized patient with alcohol abuse, findings are consistent with numerous Pappenheimer bodies due to asplenia together with alcohol-related disturbance of iron utilization; bone marrow examination for ring sideroblasts may be considered.

ddx.vs: Stippling is diffuse throughout the cell and is Prussian blue negative, whereas these granules stain blue with iron stain.
Howell-Jolly bodies are single round DNA remnants that remain unstained with Prussian blue.
Heinz bodies are invisible on Wright stain and require supravital crystal violet or brilliant cresyl blue staining.
Parasites show ring forms with cytoplasm and chromatin dots rather than clustered iron granules, and are iron negative.
